findings.title: Org-agnostic `requireAdmin` lets a tenant admin read other tenants' admin data
evidence: apps/api/src/middleware/admin.ts:49-58 — org-pinned requests require an admin role IN the pinned org unless the caller holds a super_admin role; single-org `admin` cannot widen scope by supplying another tenant's id
apps/api/src/lib/admin-scope.ts:28-60 — resolveAdminTenantScope: allTenants requires BOTH profile.is_super_admin AND a cross-tenant role key; orgIds is the approved membership list
apps/api/src/lib/admin-scope.ts:70-99 — applyOrgScope fails closed (NO_ORG_MATCH sentinel); applyRequestedOrg rejects a requested org outside the caller's approved set
apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:26-35, apps/api/src/routes/dashboard.ts:19-50, apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:32-79, apps/api/src/routes/business-os.ts:41-86 — all apply the shared tenant predicate
apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:169-182 — organizations list scoped by the same helper (removed the old super_admin-flag-OR-admin-role disjunction)
apps/api/src/__tests__/organizations.test.ts:155-246 — tests scope a plain admin to own orgs and show all orgs only for flag+role
apps/api/src/__tests__/organizations.test.ts:374-410 — cross-tenant domain writes return 403
findings.impact: A tenant-scoped admin could previously enumerate and read other tenants' admin data (organizations, audit trails, dashboards, search). The fix closes the main read paths; no regression found at 8d299b8d.
findings.recommendation: Keep the shared admin-scope helper as the single decision point; add a regression test asserting that every new `requireAdmin` read route either calls resolveAdminTenantScope/applyOrgScope or uses requireOrgAccessByParam.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: middleware/admin.ts org-pinned branch, admin-scope.ts helpers and the scoped audit/dashboard/search/business-os/organizations routes are all present and covered by tests (PRs #93/#127 lineage). No regression.

findings.title: Impersonation/cross-tenant access is logged but not reviewable or alerted
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:122-153 — GET /api/v1/audit/impersonation lists impersonation_log; gated on resolveAdminTenantScope().allTenants (403 otherwise)
apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:168-191 — GET /api/v1/audit/impersonation/export, same allTenants gate
apps/api/src/services/impersonation.ts:8-49 — every cross-tenant entry (org-access middleware, tenant.ts, service-role) writes impersonation_log
apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:125-127,252-255 — portal_impersonation_events_total counter incremented per event
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:45-56 — alert rule 'Elevated cross-tenant (impersonation) access volume' (>0.5 events/s over 10m) pointing operators at the review endpoint
apps/api/src/__tests__/audit.test.ts:248-346 — tests for list/export, single-org denial and org filter
findings.impact: Cross-tenant access is now reviewable via API and alertable via Prometheus; previously it was only a raw table nobody queried.
findings.recommendation: Add a web admin page for the impersonation trail and audit the impersonation export itself (see the exports finding residual); keep the alert rule threshold reviewed.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: review endpoints, metric and alert rule present with tests. Residual (tracked under the export-audit finding): no web UI page, and /audit/impersonation/export writes no audit event.

findings.title: Sensitive admin exports are not audit-logged
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:84, apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:81, apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:96 — tickets/projects/audit exports now write an *.export event (row count only) — PR #127 / 24aa512a
apps/api/src/routes/approvals.ts:78, assets.ts:59, domain-monitors.ts:56, findings.ts:63, proposals.ts:63 — the five modules that already logged exports
apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:168-191 — GET /audit/impersonation/export: no logAuditEvent before sendExportResponse (the most sensitive export in the system)
apps/api/src/routes/satisfaction-pulse-widget.ts:81-110 — GET /satisfaction-pulse/export: no audit event
apps/api/src/routes/client-onboarding-command-center.ts:71-110 — GET /client-onboarding/export.csv: no audit event
apps/api/src/routes/dynamic-client-forms-builder.ts:65-78 — GET /dynamic-forms/export.csv: no audit event
apps/api/src/lib/csv.ts:47-72 — sendExportResponse itself performs no logging
findings.impact: Exports of tenant data (tickets, projects, audit trail, satisfaction feedback, onboarding records) are largely auditable, but the platform-level impersonation trail export and three module exports leave no audit trail, so exfiltration of those datasets is not attributable from audit_logs alone.
findings.recommendation: Route every export through a helper that writes the *.export audit event (actor, entity, row count, filters) before streaming; add a test per export route.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: PR #127 (24aa512a) fix present for tickets/projects/audit and the five pre-existing modules; residual: impersonation/export (audit.ts:168), satisfaction-pulse, client-onboarding and dynamic-forms exports are still un-audited. CHANGELOG.md:252-254 claims 'Every sensitive export is audit-logged' — over-broad.

findings.title: Destructive deletes are inconsistently confirmation-gated and org delete is unrecoverable
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/delete-confirm.ts:8-16 — assertDeleteConfirmed requires a { confirm: true } body
grep -rn 'router.delete(' apps/api/src/routes | wc -l → 59 DELETE handlers; only 4 call assertDeleteConfirmed: api-keys.ts:148, documents.ts:567, tickets.ts:494, webhook-management.ts:374

apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:403-429 — DELETE /organizations/:id has NO confirm body, hard-deletes the organization and cascades to all tenant tables (FKs `on delete cascade`, e.g. bootstrap lines 138,203,223,233,284,307,328,343,370,394,410,455,489,512,523,540,560,578,591)

apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:1018-1055 (document share delete), apps/api/src/routes/batch.ts:143-163, apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:333-351, apps/api/src/routes/approvals.ts:302-330, apps/api/src/routes/roles.ts:185-216 — hard deletes with no confirmation body
supabase/migrations/5302432_drop_unused_soft_delete_columns.sql:1-32 — soft-delete columns were removed; product decision is HARD delete
docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:64-76 — recovery of an accidental delete depends on reverse migration/PITR/S3 backup; no in-row restore
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/organizations/[orgId]/page.tsx:1-318 — no organization delete control in the web UI (API-only destructive path)
findings.impact: A single authenticated DELETE of an organization destroys every cascaded tenant row with no typed confirmation and no in-app recovery; other destructive endpoints vary between typed confirmations, UI dialogs and no confirmation at all, so operator error risk is uneven and hard to reason about.
findings.recommendation: Require the confirmation body (or an elevation token) on every destructive DELETE, add a typed org-name/slug confirmation for organization delete, and either restore soft-delete for organizations or document the PITR-only recovery in the admin UI; add a CI check that new DELETE routes call assertDeleteConfirmed.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: unchanged since 9c0b88c — 4/59 confirmations, org delete still unconfirmed + cascading + hard-delete. Impact raised by the cascade evidence.

findings.title: Bulk document operations apply without a per-row preview or elevation guardrail
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:651-695 — POST /documents/bulk/folder: applies folder_path to every owned id; no dry-run/preview endpoint, no before/after diff
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:697-751 — POST /documents/bulk/metadata: applies description/folder/visibility (visibility can flip documents to `public`) with no preview
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:651,697 — both routes use requirePermission('documents','create'), not a dedicated bulk/elevated permission or a second confirmation
apps/web/components/admin/AdminDocumentsBulkControls.tsx:141-335 — modal shows only the selected count and the target values; no per-row preview of what will change
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/import-export/actions.ts:46-80 — store catalog JSON import applies immediately (created/updated counts after the fact), no dry-run
apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:555-600 — ticket bulk status/priority update likewise applies immediately (org pre-filtered, audit-logged)
findings.impact: An operator can flip many documents (including visibility to public) or import a whole catalog from one action without seeing the affected rows or the diff; a mistake is only visible after the fact and has no undo.
findings.recommendation: Add a preview/dry-run that returns the resolved row set and field diffs, require a second explicit apply step (or typed confirmation) for visibility/ownership-changing bulk ops, and consider a dedicated `documents:bulk` permission.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: no preview/dry-run added; audit events record ids+counts only (documents.ts:679-689,735-745). Bulk ops are org-filtered and audited (strengths), but the preview/elevation gap remains.

findings.title: Bulk invite creates pre-confirmed auth accounts (and org onboarding auto-approves admin)
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/bulk.ts:108-116 — supabase.auth.admin.createUser({ email, password: <random 16 chars>, email_confirm: true }) — account is created confirmed and no invite email carries the password
apps/api/src/routes/bulk.ts:145-151 — membership inserted with status 'pending'
apps/api/src/routes/bulk.ts:35-48 — roleId is any non-empty string (no check that the role is assignable or tenant-scoped)

apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:118-127 — POST /organizations/onboard inserts the new admin's membership with status 'approved' (auto-approval) and adminRoleKey from the request (validators/organization.ts:31-40, default client_admin)
apps/web/components/admin/BulkInviteForm.tsx:24-45 — client parses the CSV and submits directly; results shown only after the import (no preview/confirmation step)
docs/ADMIN_FEATURES.md:110-135 — documents the confirmed-email/random-password behavior
findings.impact: Bulk import silently creates confirmed auth identities with unknown passwords (account-takeover surface if the email inbox is later compromised; no consent email), and org onboarding can auto-approve a membership with an operator-chosen role — including cross-tenant role keys (see the role-assignment finding).
findings.recommendation: Use inviteUserByEmail (or set email_confirm false + password reset) for bulk invites; require an explicit approval step for onboarding admin memberships (or at least restrict adminRoleKey to tenant-scoped roles); add a preview step listing the emails/roles before apply.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: bulk.ts:114 still creates email_confirm:true accounts with a never-delivered random password; organizations.ts:124 still auto-approves; roleId/adminRoleKey unvalidated (cross-ref new P1 role-assignment finding).

findings.title: No rate limiting specific to expensive/destructive admin operations
evidence: apps/api/src/app.ts:125-147 — global IP limiter 300/15min and per-user limiter 600/15min (rateLimitByUser) cover the whole API
apps/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts:27-40 — rateLimitByUser: 600 requests/15min per bearer-token hash
apps/api/src/routes/bulk.ts:69-79 — bulk invite caps 500 entries per request but nothing caps request frequency; 600 req/15min ≈ up to 300k auth-user creations per user per window

No route-specific limiter exists on /documents/bulk/*, /tickets/bulk, /audit/export (10k rows), /audit/impersonation/export, /organizations/:id (delete) or /bulk/invite — grep for rateLimit usage shows only auth routes and admin/test-email (admin.ts:54)
docs/API_RATE_LIMITING.md:1-40 — documents only the two global limiters
findings.impact: A single admin or a compromised admin token can hammer expensive exports, bulk mutations and org deletion far beyond normal operator usage; there is no second line of defense or operator-facing guardrail for destructive endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Add per-route limiters (or a dedicated 'dangerous admin operations' limiter keyed by user+route) for bulk invite, bulk document ops, exports and organization delete; surface 429s in the admin UI and add tests.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: only the two global limiters + rateLimitEmail on admin/test-email exist; unchanged since 9c0b88c.

findings.title: No undo/soft-delete is exercised despite the schema supporting it
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302432_drop_unused_soft_delete_columns.sql:1-32 — drops deleted_at/deleted_by from tickets/projects/documents and states the product decision is HARD delete; columns were never written or read
docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:64-76 — 'Deletion semantics: hard delete (no soft-delete columns)'; recovery depends on reverse migration/PITR/S3 restore
git merge-base --is-ancestor 925ec007 9c0b88c → true; git show 925ec007 — the drop migration was already an ancestor of the previous run's commit
supabase/migrations/5302109_soft_delete.sql:1-17 — original (now removed) soft-delete columns
findings.impact: The misleading tombstone schema is gone and hard-delete recovery is documented, so operators no longer assume deletes are restorable; the residual risk is that recovery is only via PITR/backup, which is a separate drill domain.
findings.recommendation: Keep the hard-delete decision documented in operator docs; if soft delete is ever revisited it must be end-to-end (writes set deleted_at, reads+RLS filter, restore UI).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: columns dropped by 5302432 (925ec007) and hard-delete documented in ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md §3. NOTE: the previous register row said 'still open — columns exist' at 9c0b88c, which was already false at that commit (the drop landed 2026-10-02, before 9c0b88c); the previous note was stale/incorrect.

findings.title: Web admin gate accepts a broader role set than the API `requireAdmin` (guard/API divergence)
evidence: apps/web/lib/roles.ts:16-31 — PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEYS has 8 keys (super_admin, admin, dispatcher, engineer, security-analyst, project-manager, finance, onboarding-specialist); isPlatformAdminKey gates the admin portal UI
apps/web/lib/auth/admin.ts:40-47 — requireAdminAccess admits any of the 8 keys
apps/api/src/lib/roles.ts:22-29 — CROSS_TENANT_KEYS = ['super_admin','admin'] only; middleware/admin.ts:40-44 uses isCrossTenantKey
apps/web/lib/roles.ts:1-15 — comment now documents that the web list is a portal-access gate only and cross-tenant reach is decided by apps/api/src/lib/admin-scope.ts
findings.impact: Dispatchers/engineers/etc. can open admin pages whose API calls then 403, producing confusing UX and repeated failed attempts in audit logs; the divergence is now documented as intentional and the API is the enforcement point, so security impact is bounded.
findings.recommendation: Either align the web gate with the API admin tiers (or derive the portal role list from the API /me/permissions), or render read-only/403 states explicitly; add a test asserting the two key lists stay in sync.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: divergence persists (8 web keys vs 2 API cross-tenant keys) but is now documented and API-enforced; severity stays P3.

findings.title: Active-org cookie setter performs no server-side authorization
evidence: apps/web/lib/org-actions.ts:8-18 — setActiveOrg(organizationId) sets the mct_active_org cookie with no check that the caller is a member of that org or a platform admin
apps/web/lib/auth/membership.ts:43-88 — the cookie is honored for admin/super_admin memberships (ad-hoc membership) and otherwise ignored for membership resolution

apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:72-126,177-231 — the API resolves the cookie/header org and validates membership; cross-tenant switches by admin/super_admin roles are audited as impersonation (org-access.ts:194-204, 111-126)
apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:44-60 — checkOrgAccess denies non-members without a cross-tenant role
findings.impact: A user can set an arbitrary org id in their cookie, but the API pins them to a real membership or 403s (cross-tenant access is impersonation-logged), so the risk is limited to UI confusion and a misleading ad-hoc membership for admins.
findings.recommendation: Validate in setActiveOrg that the caller has an approved membership in the org (or is a platform admin) before writing the cookie; return a typed error otherwise.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: setter still unguarded; risk bounded by API-side org-access enforcement + impersonation logging. No fix targeted at the setter itself.

findings.title: Admin global search and dashboard expose global resource names/counts to any admin
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:32-79 — resolves caller memberships + is_super_admin; allTenants requires BOTH; every entity query is scoped to scopedOrgIds when not allTenants
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:113-163 — users, tickets, projects, documents and organizations queries all receive the org predicate (organizations previously unscoped)
apps/api/src/routes/dashboard.ts:19-50 — every count (organizations/tickets/projects/documents/pending memberships) passes through applyOrgScope
apps/api/src/__tests__/organizations.test.ts:155-246, apps/api/src/__tests__/search-tenant-scope.test.ts — tenant scoping tests
findings.impact: A plain tenant admin can no longer enumerate other tenants' names or global counts; only a genuine cross-tenant admin (profile flag + role) sees the global view.
findings.recommendation: Keep the shared scope helper on all admin aggregate surfaces; add a regression test when new entities are added to search.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: search and dashboard apply resolveAdminTenantScope/applyOrgScope with tests; fixed as part of the ADMIN-P1-001 hardening.

findings.title: Global store catalog is mutable by any tenant admin
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/store/catalog.ts:160-168,355-360 — a single-org admin's product/category rows are pinned to their own org; only a genuine allTenants admin can write global (organization_id NULL) rows
apps/api/src/routes/store/catalog.ts:189-202,248-257,317-326 — upsert/update/delete reject rows whose organization_id does not match the caller's allowed org
apps/api/src/routes/store/catalog.ts:428-437,487-496 — same guard for categories
supabase/migrations/5302408_store_tenant_scoping.sql — store tenant-scoping migration (MT-P0-003)
findings.impact: Tenant admins can no longer overwrite or delete the global storefront catalog; they can only manage rows belonging to their own org.
findings.recommendation: Keep the org-pin helper for catalog writes; add tests covering cross-tenant product/category upsert and delete.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: catalog writes are org-pinned (MT-P0-003 fix) with explicit per-row ownership checks; global rows are cross-tenant-admin only.

findings.title: Role assignment paths let a delegated user-manager grant cross-tenant admin roles (self-escalation)
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/memberships.ts:123-156 — PATCH /memberships/:id accepts any roleId (validators/membership.ts:3-8) and updates it with NO guard on cross-tenant role keys and no self-assignment block

apps/api/src/routes/users.ts:390-442 — PATCH /users/:id/role blocks assigning `super_admin` unless the caller's profile.is_super_admin, but does NOT guard the `admin` role key and does not block self-assignment
apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:77-127 — POST /organizations/onboard accepts an arbitrary adminRoleKey (validators/organization.ts:31-40) and inserts an APPROVED membership with it
apps/api/src/routes/bulk.ts:35-48 — bulk invite accepts an arbitrary roleId for a pending membership
apps/api/src/lib/roles.ts:22-29 — CROSS_TENANT_KEYS = ['super_admin','admin']; a membership with either key is cross-tenant
apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:44-60,111-126 — ANY approved membership whose role key is admin/super_admin grants cross-tenant access to every org (logged as impersonation, not blocked)
apps/api/src/middleware/permissions.ts:70-86 — admin/super_admin role keys bypass requirePermission entirely

supabase/migrations/5302424_manage_actions.sql:1-29 — users:manage and roles:manage are explicitly added so they are 'satisfiable and delegable' (granted to super_admin/admin; grantable to custom roles via the role editor)
apps/api/src/routes/roles.ts:252-302 — PUT /roles/:id/permissions lets a roles:manage holder add any catalog permission (incl. users:manage) to any role except super_admin's
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/users/[userId]/page.tsx:176-187 — the admin UI role dropdown lists every role (including super_admin) with no client-side restriction
findings.impact: A user delegated only user/role management (users:manage or roles:manage, e.g. a custom 'helpdesk admin' role) can assign themselves or another account the `admin` role key (or via memberships.patch the `super_admin` key) and thereby gain cross-tenant read/write reach over every tenant plus full permission bypass. The change is audited (membership.update / user.role.update) but only after the fact; there is no preventive control.
findings.recommendation: Centralize role-assignment authorization in one helper (e.g. assertCanAssignRole): assigning any CROSS_TENANT_KEYS role requires profile.is_super_admin; block self-role changes for non-super-admins; validate roleId against an assignable allowlist per caller; apply it to memberships POST/PATCH, users PATCH /role, bulk invite and organizations/onboard; add negative tests for each path.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d (self-privilege-escalation special check). Precondition: caller must hold users:manage or roles:manage (only admin/super_admin by default, but explicitly delegable per 5302424 and the role editor). Cross-refs: CHAIN-P2-003 (capability escalation) may overlap; the users.ts super_admin guard shows the intended policy that memberships.ts does not enforce.

findings.title: Approval flows allow self-approval and cancellation of already-approved requests
evidence: apps/api/src/services/approvals.ts:68-118 — approveRequest sets status approved with no check that approvedBy !== existing.requested_by (no segregation of duties)
apps/api/src/routes/approvals.ts:332-365 — POST /approvals/:id/approve only requires requirePermission('approvals','edit'); a requester with that permission can approve their own request
apps/api/src/services/approvals.ts:169-193 — cancelRequest has NO status guard (unlike approve/reject at lines 78,130) so an already-approved request can be moved to 'cancelled' afterwards
apps/api/src/routes/approvals.ts:402-435 — POST /approvals/:id/cancel exposes that path
No test asserts self-approval rejection (apps/api/src/__tests__/approvals.test.ts)
findings.impact: The approval module can be used as a rubber stamp: the same operator can request and approve a privileged change, and an approved decision can be silently reversed to cancelled, weakening the four-eyes intent of the workflow. Both actions are audit-logged, but the control itself does not enforce separation.
findings.recommendation: Reject approve/reject when the actor is the requester (configurable, at minimum for privileged request types); restrict cancel to pending requests (or record a reversal event with reason); add tests for both.

findings.title: Destructive deletes are not consistently audit-logged
evidence: grep/scan of apps/api/src/routes: 59 DELETE handlers; 7 perform a hard delete with no logAuditEvent: client-onboarding-command-center.ts:174-190, dynamic-client-forms-builder.ts:139-150, edu-automation.ts:598-613 (phishing target), license-optimizer.ts:195-206, projects.ts:333-351 (project sub-resources), status-page.ts:249-264, uptime-monitor.ts:220-233
Contrast — deletes that ARE audited: tickets.ts:492-525, organizations.ts:417-422, documents.ts:589-595, api-keys.ts:166-171, webhook-management.ts:388-394, roles.ts:203-209, memberships.ts:166-171
apps/api/src/services/audit.ts:22-67 — logAuditEvent retries 3x and logs 'audit trail gap' on final failure
supabase/migrations/5302026...v3.sql:1683-1700 — audit_logs has select/insert policies only; no delete policy, so the trail is append-only (but gaps cannot be reconstructed)
findings.impact: Deletions in those modules leave no audit trail, so an insider deleting records (e.g. uptime checks, license allocations, onboarding records, phishing targets) cannot be reconstructed from audit_logs; the special check 'audit logs for delete actions' fails for these routes.
findings.recommendation: Add logAuditEvent to the seven missing DELETE handlers (or a shared audited-delete helper), and add a CI/test guard that every router.delete handler either logs an audit event or is explicitly exempted.

findings.title: Any org member can open the Stripe billing portal for their org (no billing-contact check)
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:383-447 — POST /billing/create-portal-session requires only requireOrgAccess (no requirePermission); the inline comment at 378-382 documents the choice because the catalog grants no billing:manage to client roles
apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:394-405 — resolves the org from body/query/X-Active-Org/cookie and creates a Stripe billing-portal session for that org's customer
apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:207-231 — POST /billing/sync (a comparable mutation) DOES require requirePermission('billing','manage') and scope checks
apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:436-441 — the session creation is audit-logged (billing.portal_session) but not blocked
Membership flags exist for this purpose: memberships.is_billing_contact (apps/api/src/routes/memberships.ts:129-139)
findings.impact: Any member of an organization (e.g. a client_user with portal access) can open the Stripe billing portal for their org and cancel/change subscriptions or payment methods — financial/business impact and an abuse path for a compromised low-privilege account; the billing-contact flag is not consulted.
findings.recommendation: Gate the portal session on is_billing_contact (or a new client-facing billing permission), or configure the Stripe portal to a restricted action set; add tests for member vs billing-contact access.

report:
# Admin Console Abuse Case Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive (full hardening rerun)
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech` (read-only worktree at `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`)
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8dc271c410b9ae2ceeda3d2c6c997af8fd` (`8d299b8d`)
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: domain subagent (26_admin_console_abuse_case_audit)
- Area code: ADMIN
- Output path (pack convention): `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/{run}/26_admin_console_abuse_case_audit.md`
- Scope limitations: read-only static review; no runtime/API execution, no production access, no lab. Rate-limit and Stripe behavior assessed from code/config only.

## Scope

Reviewed: admin/organization/user/role APIs and web admin UI; destructive deletes; confirmations; bulk invite; bulk document/ticket operations; approval flows; impersonation logging and review; billing panel entry points; webhook/API-key admin; admin settings; exports; audit logging of role/delete/export actions; tests covering these.

Not reviewed in depth (owned by other domains): RLS policy design (37), multi-tenant attack simulation (25), billing reconciliation (29), file upload/download (28), webhook delivery/replay (27), secrets/CI/infra.

## Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts` (90 lines) | API | Super-admin tenant list + test-email | GET /organizations gated on `profiles.is_super_admin`; test-email rate-limited + audited |
| `apps/api/src/middleware/admin.ts` | API | `requireAdmin` org-pinning | Lines 49-58: pinned org requires admin in that org unless super_admin |

## Executive Summary

The admin surface is materially safer than at the previous run. The ADMIN-P1-001 org-scoping fix is intact and broadly applied (audit, dashboard, search, business-os, organizations, approvals/assets/projects/tickets exports), impersonation is now reviewable and alerted, exports were mostly brought under audit logging, and the store catalog is org-pinned. The web admin gate is consistently applied to all 203 admin pages.

Remaining risk concentrates in four places. (1) **Role assignment has no cross-tenant-role guard** on the memberships/onboard paths: a delegated `users:manage`/`roles:manage` holder can assign themselves the `admin`/`super_admin` role key and gain cross-tenant reach plus permission bypass — the users.ts guard proves the policy exists but is not enforced everywhere. (2) **Destructive actions are unevenly protected**: only 4 of 59 DELETE handlers require a confirmation body, organization delete cascades to all tenant data with no confirmation and no in-app recovery, and 7 deletes leave no audit event. (3) **Approvals can be self-approved** and approved requests can be cancelled afterwards. (4) **Bulk operations (documents, store import, bulk invite) apply without preview/dry-run**, and bulk invite still creates pre-confirmed accounts with a never-delivered password while onboarding auto-approves admin memberships. A minor billing-panel gap (any org member can open the Stripe portal) rounds out the abuse-case set.

Recommended next actions: fix the role-assignment policy first (P1), then add confirmation + audit to destructive endpoints, a self-approval guard, and export audit coverage for the four remaining exports.

## Findings

1. **Org-agnostic `requireAdmin` lets a tenant admin read other tenants' admin data** — P1, `verified-fixed`. Org-pinning + shared scope helper present with tests.
2. **Impersonation/cross-tenant access is logged but not reviewable or alerted** — P1, `verified-fixed`. Review endpoints + metric + Prometheus alert present; residual UI/export gaps tracked below.
3. **Sensitive admin exports are not audit-logged** — P2, `partially-fixed`. Tickets/projects/audit now audited (PR #127); impersonation/export + satisfaction-pulse + onboarding + dynamic-forms still not.
4. **Destructive deletes are inconsistently confirmation-gated and org delete is unrecoverable** — P2, `still-open`. 4/59 confirmed; org delete cascades with no confirm or undo.
5. **Bulk document operations apply without a per-row preview or elevation guardrail** — P2, `still-open`.
6. **Bulk invite creates pre-confirmed auth accounts (and org onboarding auto-approves admin)** — P2, `still-open`.
7. **No rate limiting specific to expensive/destructive admin operations** — P2, `still-open`.
8. **No undo/soft-delete is exercised despite the schema supporting it** — P2, `verified-fixed`. Columns dropped (5302432), hard delete documented; previous register note was stale.
9. **Web admin gate accepts a broader role set than the API `requireAdmin` (guard/API divergence)** — P3, `still-open` (documented, API-enforced).
10. **Active-org cookie setter performs no server-side authorization** — P3, `still-open` (API-side enforcement bounds impact).
11. **Admin global search and dashboard expose global resource names/counts to any admin** — P3, `verified-fixed`.
12. **Global store catalog is mutable by any tenant admin** — P3, `verified-fixed`.
13. **Role assignment paths let a delegated user-manager grant cross-tenant admin roles (self-escalation)** — P1, `open` (new).
14. **Approval flows allow self-approval and cancellation of already-approved requests** — P2, `open` (new).
15. **Destructive deletes are not consistently audit-logged** — P2, `open` (new).
16. **Any org member can open the Stripe billing portal for their org (no billing-contact check)** — P2, `open` (new).

### D. Guardrail recommendations (operator-facing)

1. Treat `admin`/`super_admin` assignment as a platform action: require a profile-flagged super admin and log the change with actor/target/role.
2. Make every destructive API require a confirmation body; org delete additionally a typed slug.
3. Require preview → apply for bulk operations; treat visibility/ownership changes as elevated.
4. Surface the impersonation trail and destructive-action audit events in the admin console.
5. Add per-route rate limits and 429 messaging for exports/bulk/destructive endpoints.
6. Keep the hard-delete decision visible in operator docs; link PITR recovery steps from the admin console.
